_note: Representative hosted text-LLM API prices, USD per 1M tokens. 'input'/'output' are official list prices (short-context tier); 'usd_per_1m' is a blended figure = (3×input + output) / 4, weighting input ~3:1 for typical RAG/agentic usage — it's the single number fed into the calculator's self-host-vs-API comparison. Real cost depends on your input:output mix; override with your own quote in the UI. Open-hosted rows are order-of-magnitude estimates (provider/quantization vary). Standard list prices as of 2026-07; closed-model prices change often.
_note_media: Per-item prices for hosted image/video generation. IMAGE presets are USD per image, quoted from the vendor's own per-image figures. VIDEO presets are USD per SECOND (the unit video APIs actually bill in); the calculator multiplies by the clip length implied by your frame count and fps, so a 10s clip costs twice a 5s one. Pick the tier that matches what your self-hosted model actually produces — comparing a 20B DiT at 50 steps against a vendor's cheapest low-quality tier is not a like-for-like comparison, and neither is comparing it against 4K. OpenAI figures are from the image-generation guide's per-image table (gpt-image-2 bills image output tokens at $30/1M; note their own table shows a larger non-square resolution can cost LESS than 1024x1024). Google figures are from the Gemini API pricing page. All video models listed by Google include audio by default.

_note_speech: Per-MINUTE prices for hosted speech APIs, USD per minute of audio — the unit STT/TTS vendors actually bill in. Derived from the curated table in data/speech.json (2026-07 official list prices); hourly quotes were divided by 60 and are marked. Rows priced per audio-token or per character do not convert to a per-minute figure without assuming a speaking rate, so they are omitted rather than estimated. Override with your own quote in the UI.
